paper_metadata.title: Brain Oscillatory Activity during Tactile Stimulation Correlates with Cortical Thickness of Intact Areas and Predicts Outcome in Post-Traumatic Comatose Patients

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a detailed description of the clinical characteristics and recruitment setting (Burdenko National Medical Research Center). However, the sample size is very small (n=10), and it is a convenience sample of patients available during a specific window, which may not fully represent the broader TBI comatose population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 10 severe TBI patients (eight males and two females) aged 37.8 ± 29.8 years (M ± 2σ) participated in the study via inpatient observation at the N. N. Burdenko National Scientific and Practical Center for Neurosurgery from 2017 to 2018.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the age, sex, and clinical setting of the target population.

items.evidence_snippet: Patients were recruited for the EEG study within 12–48 h after MRI.
items.reasoning: While the timing relative to MRI is clear, the specific sampling frame (e.g., consecutive vs. convenience) is not explicitly stated.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The EEG measurement (the prognostic factor) is highly standardized, using a clear protocol for tactile stimulation and objective Fast Fourier Transform analysis. The same equipment and settings were used for all participants.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG was acquired using a 19-channel EEG amplifier... Fast Fourier transform was used to analyze power spectral density (PSD).
items.reasoning: The prognostic factor (EEG oscillatory response) is clearly defined by its technical parameters.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The sampling rate was 250 Hz. The amplifier bandpass filter was nominally set to 0.05–70 Hz. Silver chloride (AgCl) electrodes... were placed according to the International 10–20 system.
items.reasoning: Standardized clinical EEG protocols were followed.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: PSD values were averaged for all 19 electrodes for each 1 Hz width frequency interval from 2 to 20 Hz
items.reasoning: The study uses continuous spectral density data rather than arbitrary categorical cut-offs.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (GOSe) is a standard clinical scale, but the timing of the outcome assessment is not standardized (it varies based on hospital stay), and there is no mention of whether the clinicians assigning the GOSe score were blinded to the EEG results.

items.reasoning: The scale is defined, but the specific time point (e.g., 6 months post-injury) is not standardized across the group.
